cross_domain_concepts.name: sieve_of_eratosthenes_adaptation
cross_domain_concepts.description: Adapt prime sieve methodology: precompute which residue classes mod 2^k have guaranteed short trajectories, eliminating them from full computation.
cross_domain_concepts.implementation_hypothesis: Build a 2^20 sieve table mapping each residue to its minimum guaranteed trajectory length. Numbers with residue in the bottom 99% are skipped.

cross_domain_concepts.name: parallel_prefix_scan
cross_domain_concepts.description: Use parallel prefix scan (Blelloch scan) to batch-process Collatz steps across many numbers simultaneously using SIMD-like operations on numpy arrays.
cross_domain_concepts.implementation_hypothesis: Represent N numbers as a numpy int64 array. Apply vectorized even/odd masks and bulk operations for each step until all converge below threshold.

cross_domain_concepts.name: random_walk_stopping_time
cross_domain_concepts.description: Model Collatz iteration as biased random walk: each step multiplies by 3/2 (prob ~log2/log3) or 1/2 (prob ~1 - log2/log3). Expected stopping time ~ C * log(n) where C ≈ log(4/3)/log(2).
cross_domain_concepts.implementation_hypothesis: Compute expected delay for each bit-length using the Kontorovich-Miller model. Flag numbers whose actual delay exceeds 3 standard deviations as interesting outliers.

cross_domain_concepts.name: finite_state_transducer
cross_domain_concepts.description: Model k Collatz steps as a finite state transducer operating on the binary representation of n. The state encodes carry propagation, and the output is the transformed number.
cross_domain_concepts.implementation_hypothesis: For k=32, build a transducer with 2^32 states. Each state maps (residue mod 2^32) to (multiplier a, offset b) such that after 32 steps: result = (a*n + b) >> 32.

cross_domain_concepts.name: entropy_guided_candidate_selection
cross_domain_concepts.description: Compute Shannon entropy of the parity sequence for the first k steps (determined by n mod 2^k). High-entropy parity sequences correlate with long trajectories.
cross_domain_concepts.implementation_hypothesis: For k=20, compute parity sequences for all 2^20 residues. Rank by entropy. Verify that known delay records cluster in top 0.1% of entropy ranking.

cross_domain_concepts.name: trajectory_compression
cross_domain_concepts.description: Encode Collatz trajectories as binary parity sequences (0=even step, 1=odd step). These compress well with run-length encoding due to the bias toward even steps.
cross_domain_concepts.implementation_hypothesis: Store only the parity sequence and starting value. Trajectory can be reconstructed deterministically. Enables compact storage of millions of trajectories for analysis.

cross_domain_concepts.name: extreme_value_theory_prediction
cross_domain_concepts.description: Model the distribution of delay record values using Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) theory. Predict where the next delay record should appear.
cross_domain_concepts.implementation_hypothesis: Fit GEV distribution to the 18 known a(n) values from A284668. Extrapolate to predict a(19) range and expected delay.
